edition.name: 'Franklin's Way to Wealth, or, Poor Richard Improved', printed by and for W. and T. Darton, 58 Holborn Hill, London, 1810, Project Gutenberg eBook #43855, released 1 October 2013, produced by Chris Curnow, Emmy and the Online Distributed Proofreading Team
edition.status: The file names its printer and year on the title page: W. and T. Darton, London, 1810, with plates dated 1805. It opens with a publisher's advertisement, an unsigned introduction in the publisher's voice and a list of other titles, then Franklin's speech in four numbered sections with a closing paragraph signed Richard Saunders. The unsigned introduction and the advertisements are not Franklin's and are not used. The Darton text may differ from the wording Franklin first published in the 1758 almanac preface. The workbook quotes this printing only. No named editor or illustrator appears in the file, so Franklin is the only contributor whose death year counts. An anonymous introduction from 1810 is long out of any term [to confirm].

modernisation.knownIssue: The double-hyphen rule writes a comma and a space. Where the printed dash followed a full stop, a question mark or a closing quotation mark, the comma lands after it (eight cases, for example 'today.", If you were a servant'). There are no doubled commas. No quotation in the workbook crosses any of them.
modernisation.outsideTheRules: Franklin's spelling (labour, plow, expences, gaol) stays as printed inside quotations. The workbook's own prose is en-GB. The rules do not touch the plural 'to-morrows' in the line 'One to-day is worth two to-morrows', so that line is not quoted; the workbook quotes the sentence before it.
modernisation.editorial: No [Editorial] changes were made. Quotations are exact, checked by section against the modernised copy.

workbookUse: the speech in full, four weeks built around its themes: week 1 time (the opening address and Section I to the leisure passage), week 2 industry and self-reliance (the rest of Section I and Section II), week 3 frugality (Section III: the sale, small costs, pride and running costs), week 4 debt, prudence and limits (the debt passage of Section III, Section IV and the closing paragraph). The editor's introduction, the advertisements and the plate captions are not used.
